model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)
model_label: REIT Core AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run on the component engine: revenue x Core FFO margin, less recurring capitalised expenditures (the Core FFO -> Core AFFO bridge) = Core AFFO. Net debt is NOT deducted because Core AFFO is already after interest expense.

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 (Dec-25) property revenues, US$m, CPT_Metrics.csv (10-K FY2025; ties to the Q4-25 earnings release: $1,573.5m = $1,399.9m rental + $173.6m non-lease components). Revenue is the DRIVER line only; the flow valued is Core AFFO.
inputs.share_count_basis: FFO-diluted share count (common shares plus OP units convertible into common, the denominator Camden uses for FFO/Core FFO/Core AFFO per share), estimated at 30-Sep-2026 at 103.5m. Two derivations bracket it: (a) the Q3-2026 weighted FFO-diluted count of 103.826m, less the 0.475m shares bought back in August-September, plus the ~0.1m of that buyback already inside the weighted figure = ~103.45m; (b) 100.1m period-end common shares per the 10-Q (which excludes shares held in deferred-compensation arrangements) + ~1.85m deferred-comp shares (the gap between weighted basic and average period-end counts) + 1.66m common units and awards = ~103.6m. The prior version's 103.2m at 30-Jun was an under-estimate: the Q3 weighted count shows the quarter opened near 103.9m. The count is held FLAT. SBC is already expensed inside Core FFO, so adding dilution would double-count it. Further buybacks ($247.9m left on the authorisation) are NOT assumed, because the AFFO forgone on the capital used would roughly offset them.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO. Core AFFO comes after net interest expense, so deducting balance-sheet debt as well would charge financing twice (dcf-methods SKILL.md). total_debt and cash are recorded for leverage context only.
inputs.total_debt_note: US$m at 30-Sep-2026 (Q3-26 10-Q note 6; CPT_Metrics.csv Q3 2026): $3,921.5m unsecured + $306.8m secured; no commercial paper outstanding. Cash excludes ~$427m of California proceeds held in restricted cash by a 1031 qualified intermediary. In October 2026 the $500m 5.85% notes due Nov-2026 were repaid at par from cash and commercial paper. Leverage context only; not deducted.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 Core AFFO, US$m (Q4-25 earnings release, 8-K 2026-02-05): Core FFO $757.225m less recurring capitalised expenditures $108.174m. This is about $5.90 per FFO-diluted share. 9M-2026 Core AFFO was $457.6m, or $4.37/share (Core FFO $534.2m less $76.6m recurring capex, 104.749m weighted FFO-diluted shares; Q3-26 10-Q MD&A).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 Core FFO, US$m ($6.88/diluted share). Nareit FFO was $744.8m ($6.77). CSV FreeCashFlow is blank because XBRL carries no capex tag here. OCF of $826.6m is a GAAP cash measure, not a distributable-flow measure.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC ($16.96m FY2025, CPT_Metrics.csv from the 10-K cash-flow add-back; about 1.1% of revenue) is expensed in G&A/property expense BEFORE Core FFO, and Camden does not add it back in Core FFO or Core AFFO. It is charged once, in the flow. House and street bases coincide (the REIT convention).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $270.7m. YTD-2026 to 30-Sep: $472.8m (4.54m shares: 1.10m at $110.03 in January, 3.44m at $102.36 under the Feb-2026 $600m plan, of which 0.47m in Q3). $247.9m remains on the authorisation. Not projected.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-18T21:00:02Z NYSE regular close (Yahoo v8 chart meta)
inputs.core_affo_history_note: Sources: Q4 earnings releases (8-K exhibit 99.1) dated 2022-02-03, 2024-02-01 and 2026-02-05. FY2020-21 are 'AFFO', which predates Camden's Core definition. FY2024/FY2025 per-share values are derived as Core AFFO $m / (Core FFO $m / Core FFO per share).
inputs.nav_cross_check: At the current price the market capitalises the post-transaction portfolio at roughly a 7% implied NOI cap rate: equity (current_price x 103.5m FFO-diluted shares) plus net debt of ~$3.6bn (30-Sep notes payable $4.23bn less $169m cash and $427m of 1031 escrow) against pro-forma property NOI of ~$965m (run-rate revenue ~$1,510m x ~64% NOI margin, the FY2025 margin). Camden sold California in July 2026 for ~$1.6bn, roughly a 5% cap on our estimate of that portfolio's NOI, and bought $754.5m of Sun Belt assets at a ~5% FFO yield. On a 5.75-6.25% private-market cap, NAV is ~$115-130/share. Cross-check only, not a model input. It says the AFFO-at-9.5% model sits well below private-market value, which is the discount a public REIT carries when the 10-year Treasury is above 5%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The rate is a USD COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC: Core AFFO is post-interest and no net debt is deducted. 10-year UST 5.07% (^TNX, 2026-11-18) + 0.85 beta x 5.0% ERP = 9.3%, held at 9.5%. UNCHANGED from the prior version (10-year was 5.18%): an 11bp move in the risk-free rate is inside the rounding of the build-up; a sustained move of ~50bp either way would move it. The beta is below 1 because this is an investment-grade apartment REIT whose housing-demand revenue re-prices annually, with net debt/EBITDA ~4.5-5x. The same 9.5% applies in all three scenarios, so scenario risk sits in the flows. In line with CCI (9.5%) and below BXP (11.5%, office).
inputs.lease_treatment: Camden's own ground/office leases as lessee are immaterial. They sit in property and G&A expense inside Core FFO and are not separately modelled.
inputs.nci_treatment: The FFO-diluted share count includes the OP units (income allocated to non-controlling interests is added back in FFO), so flow and denominator are on the same basis. No separate NCI deduction.
inputs.notes: Model: REIT Core AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md (REIT row), following the house US-REIT precedent (BXP, CCI) and the ARG.NZ/PCT.NZ/IPL.NZ family. SAME MODEL as the prior (2026-09-26) valuation; this is an UPDATE for the Q3-2026 10-Q and the 2026-11-05 guidance. GAAP net income is dominated by real-estate depreciation (~$598m FY2025) and gains on sale ($973m on the California sale in Q3-26), so neither EPS nor P/E means anything here. Engine mapping: EBITDA margin = Core FFO / revenue (post-interest), D&A = 0 (real-estate D&A is already added back in FFO), capex = recurring capitalised expenditures as % of revenue (the Core FFO -> Core AFFO bridge), SBC = 0 (expensed inside Core FFO), tax = 0 (REIT distributes >=100% of taxable income), WC = 0, net_debt = 0. Development, redevelopment and acquisition capital is NOT deducted: it is growth capital funded from retained AFFO (~25% of AFFO at the $4.24 dividend) plus recycling, and the growth path is held to what that retention can fund. YEAR 1 IS A PRO-FORMA RUN-RATE YEAR, NOT the GAAP FY2026, and it is now anchored on ACTUALS rather than on the pre-close estimate. Revenue: Q3-26 property revenue was $381.1m, which still held a July stub of California (est. ~$5m; the 10-Q gives the month, not the day) and lacked part-quarter revenue on the July/August acquisitions (~$1.3m), so the Q4 run-rate is ~$377.5m, or ~$1,510m a year: -4.0% on FY2025 (prior version estimated $1,490m, -5.3%). Core FFO: Q4-26 guidance of $1.63-1.67 (mid $1.65) x 103.5m shares = ~$171m, annualised ~$683m, plus ~$3m for redeploying the $427m of 1031 escrow cash into ~5%-yield assets = ~$686m, about $6.62/share (prior version: $693m, $6.71). The step-down from Q3's $1.715 is California leaving for the full quarter and higher net interest. That is a Core FFO margin of 45.4%, and Year-1 Core AFFO of ~$581m, or $5.62/share, against a FY2026 blended estimate of ~$5.71 (9M $4.37 + Q4 Core FFO $1.65 less ~$0.31 recurring capex). WHAT CHANGED vs the prior version: anchors (price, 30-Sep balance sheet, share count 103.2m -> 103.5m), Year-1 growth in all three scenarios (+1.3pt, the higher actual revenue run-rate), and the Core FFO margin path in all three scenarios (-1.0 to -1.1pt in every year, a level shift: the post-transaction base earns less per revenue dollar than estimated, and nothing in Q3 says the gap closes). DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: growth in Years 2-10 (Q3 same-store revenue was flat and FY2026 same-store guidance of 0-1% was maintained, which is what the path already assumed; a 2027 guide outside roughly 1-2.5% same-store revenue, or new-lease spreads still below -2% in spring 2027, would move it); the shape of the margin recovery after Year 1; recurring capex at 6.9% / 6.7% / 7.2% of revenue (9M-26 ran 6.6% against 6.7% in 9M-25, the normal seasonal under-run before a heavier Q4; a full-year figure outside 6.5-7.3% would move it); the 9.5% cost of equity; terminal growth and caps; the 20/50/30 weights; the 15% hurdle. The Q3 halt of two development parcels ($86.4m impairment, excluded from FFO) trims the pipeline but four communities remain under construction with $209m to complete, so the retention-funded growth assumption is left alone. FFO/AFFO history comes from EDGAR earnings releases (CIK 906345) and the 10-Q MD&A reconciliation because the XBRL-parsed Metrics.csv carries no REIT supplemental measures.

historical_growth.eps_basis: Statutory EPS ($6.07 FY2022 -> $3.54 FY2025; $1.24 FY2020) swings on gains on sale and impairments and is not used. The relevant series is Core AFFO/share: 5.69 (FY2022) -> 5.90 (FY2025) = +1.2%/yr over 3 years; 4.13 (FY2020 AFFO) -> 5.90 = +7.4%/yr over 5 years, flattered by the pandemic trough base and the 2021-22 rent spike.
historical_growth.fcf_basis: Core AFFO in $m (the owner-flow analogue for a REIT): 622.1 (FY2022) -> 649.1 (FY2025); 418.2 (FY2020 AFFO) -> 649.1. The 5-year figure includes the 2022 consolidation of the Camden Multifamily Value-Add Funds and equity raised in 2021-22.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Long-run Core AFFO growth set at CPI-like rent growth of 2.5%, consistent with the 3-year Core AFFO/share CAGR (1.2%, depressed by the 2023-26 Sun Belt supply wave) and below the 5-year (7.4%, flattered by the trough base). Book-equity CAGR is not used: it is historical-cost depreciated book, shrinking through depreciation and buybacks, and says nothing about earning power.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-4.3% 3yr / +4.8% 5yr) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (3.4% / 8.6%) and from EPS. Expected for a depreciated-cost REIT with buybacks. Neither series is the anchor; Core AFFO/share and management guidance are.
historical_growth.notes: Core AFFO/share was flat at ~$5.90 for three years (FY2023-25) as Sun Belt new supply held new-lease rates negative. 9M-2026 Core FFO was $534.2m against $564.2m (-5.3% in dollars; $5.10 against $5.12 per share, cushioned by a 5% lower share count), and Core AFFO $457.6m against $488.8m. Q3-26 same-store revenue was -$0.4m year on year on lower rental rates. FY2026 guidance ($6.75 Core FFO mid, maintained 2026-11-05) is a ~2% decline per share. CAGRs are unchanged from the prior version because FY0 is still FY2025.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 is the pro-forma run-rate after the California exit and the Sun Belt acquisitions, now built from the Q3-26 actual ($381.1m, adjusted to a ~$377.5m Q4 run-rate; see inputs.notes): -4.0% on FY2025. Y2-Y10 are UNCHANGED from the prior version. Y2 is +2.0%: same-property revenue recovers from the 2026 0-1% guide to ~1.5% as Sun Belt deliveries fall from their 2024-25 peak, plus lease-up of the developments under construction. Y3-Y5 are 3.0-3.5% as the supply cliff lets new-lease rates turn positive. The path then fades to 2.5%, CPI-like rent growth, fundable from the ~25% of AFFO that is retained.
base.margin_rationale: Row = Core FFO / revenue. FY2025 was 48.1%; Q3-26 was 46.7% with a California stub still in it. Year 1 is 45.4%, set so Core FFO is ~$686m: Q4-26 guidance midpoint $1.65 x 103.5m shares annualised, plus ~$3m for redeploying the 1031 escrow. The fall from FY2025 is California leaving at a ~5% cap while much of the proceeds retired ~4% commercial paper or bought back shares (which cuts the share count, not the interest bill by as much), plus 2026 same-property expenses +2-3% against revenue +0-1%, higher overhead and lost fee income. The whole path sits 1.0-1.1pt below the prior version (a level shift from the lower actual base); its shape is unchanged: a Y2 dip as development capitalised interest ends and the $350m term loan and other maturities refinance near 5%, then recovery to 46.5% on operating leverage once rent growth outpaces the mostly fixed interest bill.
base.capex_rationale: Recurring capitalised expenditures (the Core FFO -> Core AFFO bridge) held at the FY2024/FY2025 actual of 6.9% of revenue ($106.4m / $1,543.8m and $108.2m / $1,573.5m). FY2023 was 6.3% and FY2022 6.4%. The sold California assets were older; the acquired Sun Belt assets average ~5 years old, which argues for a slightly lower ratio, but Gulf Coast insurance, casualty exposure and an ageing core Houston/DC book offset that.
base.tax_rationale: Zero. Camden is a REIT and distributes at least 100% of taxable income by policy (10-Q liquidity section), so Core AFFO is already after tax.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.5% / 2.5% gives ~14.6x terminal Core AFFO (a 6.8% AFFO yield) and binds below the 20x cap. Camden has historically traded at ~17-25x Core AFFO and is at the bottom of that range today on the $5.62 run-rate.

bull.growth_rationale: Y1 -3.7% is the run-rate with the California stub in Q3 at the low end of the estimate. Y2-Y10 UNCHANGED: the Sun Belt supply cliff produces a rent-growth recovery like 2011-15, new-lease rates turn positive in 2027, and the remaining 1031 proceeds and development starts are deployed accretively. Long-run growth is 3.0%, supported by in-migration to Texas, Florida and the Carolinas.
bull.margin_rationale: Year 1 at 45.6% is Q4-26 guidance at its $1.67 high end. Operating leverage on rent growth with expense growth held near 3%, and lower refinancing coupons if the 10-year eases from ~5.1%, lift the margin to 48%, back to about the FY2025 level (prior version: 49%; the 1pt level shift applies here too).
bull.capex_rationale: A younger post-recycling portfolio (acquired assets average ~5 years old) runs recurring capex slightly below the FY2025 6.9%.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.5% / 3.0% gives ~15.8x and binds below the 20x cap. Same cost of equity as base: the bull case is better flows, not a cheaper rate.

bear.growth_rationale: Y1 -4.5% is the run-rate with a larger California stub in Q3 and softer Q4 rents. Y2-Y10 UNCHANGED: supply absorption drags into 2027-28 and a Sun Belt labour-market slowdown keeps new-lease rates negative, which pushes same-property revenue to flat in Y2. Rent-control or stabilisation measures spread to Camden's jurisdictions. Long-run growth is 2.0%, below CPI in real terms, as build-to-rent single-family competition caps pricing.
bear.margin_rationale: Year 1 at 45.1% is Q4-26 guidance near its $1.63 low end. Low-coupon debt and the $350m term loan refinance at 5%+ while NOI is flat; property taxes and Gulf Coast insurance rise faster than rents, taking the margin to 43.8% (prior version 44.8%, same 1pt level shift). The $53m revenue-management settlement and the open DOJ and state actions show the legal-cost line can recur, even though Core FFO excludes it.
bear.capex_rationale: Recurring capex drifts up with insurance- and casualty-driven replacement cycles and the ageing Houston/DC core.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.5% / 2.0% gives ~13.6x and binds below the 16x cap (a ~7.3% exit AFFO yield).

scenario_narratives.base: Camden has completed its California exit: run-rate Core AFFO is about $5.62/share on 103.5m FFO-diluted shares, anchored on Q4-2026 Core FFO guidance of $1.63-1.67 and consistent with maintained FY2026 guidance of $6.75. As Sun Belt deliveries fall away, same-property revenue growth recovers from 0-1% in 2026 to ~3-3.5% in 2028-30 and then fades to CPI-like 2.5%. The Core FFO margin dips on refinancing and the end of development capitalised interest, then recovers to 46.5%. Recurring capex stays at 6.9% of revenue. Core AFFO is capitalised at a 9.5% USD cost of equity with no net-debt deduction.
scenario_narratives.bull: The supply cliff produces a 2011-15-style rent recovery: new-lease rates turn positive in 2027 and revenue grows 4.5-5% at the peak. Recycled capital earns above its ~5% FFO yield, the Core FFO margin rises to 48% on operating leverage and easier refinancing, and a younger portfolio trims recurring capex to 6.7%. Long-run growth is 3.0%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Sun Belt oversupply and a regional labour slowdown keep new-lease rates negative through 2027, so same-property revenue is flat in Y2. Refinancing at 5%+ and rising property tax and insurance compress the Core FFO margin to ~43.8%. Rent-stabilisation measures spread to Camden's jurisdictions, recurring capex creeps to 7.2%, and long-run growth settles at 2.0%. Exit at ~13.6x Core AFFO.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 20/50/30 (house default 15/50/35; bear lifted, bull trimmed). Three years of flat Core AFFO/share, FY2026 guidance down ~2%, 9M Core FFO dollars down 5%, and a 10-year Treasury above 5% make the downside a live one. It is still not a solvency case: investment-grade balance sheet, ~$0.9bn of debt retired from the California proceeds, no commercial paper outstanding at 30-Sep, and dividend cover of ~1.3x ($4.24 against ~$5.62 AFFO). The bull weight stays meaningful because Sun Belt construction starts have fallen sharply. Q3 neither confirmed nor broke the recovery thesis (same-store revenue flat, guidance maintained); spring-2027 new-lease spreads are the evidence that would move the weights.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Camden is valued as a stream of Core AFFO, which is Core FFO less recurring capitalised expenditures and is the company's own distributable-cash measure. It is capitalised at a 9.5% USD cost of equity, with no net-debt deduction because the flow is already after interest. GAAP EPS is set aside: it is dominated by real-estate depreciation and gains on sale ($973m in Q3-2026 alone). Year 1 is a pro-forma run-rate after the July-2026 California exit and $754.5m of Sun Belt acquisitions, anchored on Q4-2026 Core FFO guidance. The market capitalises run-rate Core AFFO at roughly 17x, which implies about a 9% cost of equity at 3% growth, and a ~7% cap rate on property NOI against the ~5% Camden achieved selling California. So the stock sits well below private-market NAV (~$115-130 at a 5.75-6.25% cap) but near what a 5% risk-free rate supports on a pure cash-yield basis.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: this is a long-duration income stream, so each 50bp on the 9.5% cost of equity moves the base value by roughly 7-8%, and the 10-year Treasury at ~5.1% is the dominant input.

The Year-1 base rests on one quarter of guidance. Q4-2026 Core FFO of $1.63-1.67 is annualised; if it proves conservative (Q3 beat its midpoint) the run-rate is ~1-2% too low, and each 1pt of Core FFO margin is worth ~2.6% of value.
Sun Belt supply absorption: Q3 same-store revenue was flat and rental rates were lower year on year. If the 2027 recovery slips a year, the base path converges on the bear path.
Refinancing: ~$0.5bn of contractual maturities remain in the next 12 months after the October repayment of the $500m 5.85% notes, including the $350m 364-day term loan, all refinancing near 5%.

Regulatory: rent-control and stabilisation legislation, plus revenue-management litigation ($53m class settlement paid in 2026; DOJ and state actions still open). Core FFO excludes these costs, but the cash still leaves.

Capital allocation: 2026 buybacks averaged ~$104, above today's price; ~$427m of sale proceeds sat in 1031 escrow at 30-Sep, and redeploying at a ~5% FFO yield is at best neutral against the AFFO yield on Camden's own stock. Two development parcels were written down $86m in Q3.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance v8 chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NYSE regular close); 52-week range 95.30-119.81.
data_sources.financials: CPT_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (SEC XBRL: property revenues, net income, OCF, debt, cash, shares, SBC, FY2007-Q3 2026). Core FFO, Core AFFO, recurring capex, share counts, buybacks, notes payable and the California sale from the Q3-2026 10-Q (CPT_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt: MD&A FFO reconciliation, notes 4-6, Part II item 2). Annual FFO/AFFO history from Camden earnings releases on EDGAR (CIK 906345): 8-K exhibit 99.1 of 2026-02-05, 2024-02-01 and 2022-02-03. FY2026 and Q4-2026 guidance as recorded in CPT_Analysis.json from the 2026-11-05 release.
data_sources.qualitative: CPT_Analysis.json (2026-11-19): California exit closed, leadership transition, RealPage settlement, guidance, risks.

prior_version.note: Built at 98.12 (2026-09-25 close); the shipped DCF carried 99.44 after a price refresh. Prior entry prices at the 15% hurdle: bear 40.93 / base 47.38 / bull 52.62 / weighted 47.67.

bridge.item: Anchor refresh: FFO-diluted share count 103.2m -> 103.5m at 30-Sep-2026 (net debt is not in the model, so the balance-sheet refresh has no value effect)
Driver change: Year-1 revenue run-rate $1,490m -> $1,510m from the Q3-26 actual (Y1 growth +1.3pt in every scenario)
Driver change: Core FFO margin path lowered 1.0-1.1pt in every year and scenario, anchoring Year 1 on Q4-26 guidance of $1.65

reconciliation.method_change: None. Same model, cost of equity, terminal assumptions, weights and hurdle.
reconciliation.price_move_note: The price move since the prior version does not enter intrinsic value; it only changes upside.
